output.week_summary: Three ideas are worth developing this week: how WIA uses a venue's sales conversations to shape its paid campaign, why different venue ads need different creative, and how Carmen weighs couples' language before excluding a Google search term. Publish the photography opinion first, show the creative strategy next, then close with the ELEVATE piece. Only that final Instagram piece needs an offer CTA. The geographic planning exchange and candid-photography wording are useful supporting material, but neither shows enough WIA contribution for a standalone post. The prospect's recurring-cost feedback stays internal. No founder seeds were supplied.

angles.title: What we bring from your venue sales conversations into your paid campaign
angles.audience: Venue owners investing in visibility who want couples to understand the value of their wedding experience before they inquire.
angles.core_perspective: When we build a paid campaign, we look for the explanations you're already using to help couples choose. For an all-inclusive venue, that meant recommending its existing comparison chart for the ads landing page, where couples could understand what each venue option includes while considering an inquiry.
angles.why_it_matters: An owner may already have a useful way to explain the difference between an all-inclusive wedding and a venue-only rental. WIA looks for opportunities to bring that explanation into the paid campaign earlier. This reflects Whitney's belief: "The best results rarely come from one thing. They're created when visibility, positioning, trust, messaging, and user experience are all aligned." It shifts the assumption that the full explanation belongs only in the conversation after a tour.
angles.wia_in_action: The venue owner described an existing comparison chart and how she uses it in follow-up. Whitney recommended including it on the ads landing page. The owner supplied the asset and sales insight; WIA identified another place where it could help couples decide.
angles.offer_connection: Show the strategic thinking inside ELEVATE, WIA's done-for-you Google and Meta advertising system with strategic creative, conversion tracking, ongoing optimization and LeadLock. The landing-page recommendation is one example of that work. CTA: join the ELEVATE waitlist, followed by a discovery call.
evidence_points: The venue owner said couples compare her all-inclusive offering with venue-only rentals and do not always understand the value of the included services.
She already had a comparison chart on her website and used it in pre-tour questions and post-tour follow-up.
Whitney recommended including that chart on the ads landing page.
verify_before_publishing: Confirm permission for an anonymized call example and any chart shown.
Keep chart inclusion as a recommendation unless implementation is confirmed.
angles.why_selected: This makes WIA's strategic contribution concrete and earns an ELEVATE invitation without relying on a result claim. It also moves beyond the recent general positioning content: the specific contribution is carrying an existing sales explanation into the paid campaign, rather than explaining why positioning matters.

angles.title: The ad that introduces your venue has a different job from the one that asks for a tour
angles.audience: Venue owners expanding their advertising who want to understand the reasoning behind their campaign's creative.
angles.core_perspective: We choose the creative around what we want a couple to do at that point. Introducing a venue, inviting an inquiry and giving someone a stronger reason to keep considering it each call for their own message within the venue's ad strategy.
angles.why_it_matters: The owner's question was whether the creative stays the same while targeting changes. Whitney explained why WIA gives each layer a different objective and message. That shows how we apply her belief: "For a wedding business, every touchpoint matters more." The thought shift is that creative choices follow the couple's next decision, rather than simply putting the same venue ad in front of different audiences.
angles.wia_in_action: Whitney separated client attraction, conversion and warm retargeting. She described an introduction for cold audiences, a direct invitation to inquire or book a tour, and deeper reasons to choose the venue for people who already know it.
evidence_points: The venue owner asked whether the funnel layers use separate creative or one creative with different targeting.
Whitney explained that client-attraction creative introduces the venue to cold audiences.
She distinguished conversion creative asking for an inquiry or tour from retargeting creative explaining why couples should choose the venue.
verify_before_publishing: Confirm permission for the anonymized exchange or any recording excerpt.
angles.why_selected: This is the clearest behind-the-scenes explanation of WIA's campaign decisions this week. Its central point is more specific than the recent buyer-journey and positioning pieces: why the creative itself changes with the job of the campaign. Keep this treatment rather than adding a second general post about couples needing several touchpoints.

angles.title: Couples can love your photography without knowing what to call it
angles.audience: Wedding photographers with a recognizable style who want to reach more couples suited to their work.
angles.core_perspective: We give couples room to describe photography differently from photographers. Before excluding a style-related Google search, Carmen asked whether those inquiries ever became clients. We want that decision to reflect what happens in the business, alongside the language used to describe the work.
angles.why_it_matters: A photographer can know that a style label does not describe her work while still wanting to understand the couples using it. Carmen's move was to ask about booking outcomes before recommending a search decision. It reflects Whitney's belief that "good marketing decisions start with good data." It shifts the assumption that an unfamiliar or mismatched style term is enough, on its own, to rule out a couple.
angles.wia_in_action: When the photographer raised "light and airy" as a possible negative keyword, Carmen asked what happened to inquiries using that phrase. She recommended leaving the term in play and revisiting it if search activity showed it becoming irrelevant.
evidence_points: The photographer said "light and airy" does not describe her style but questioned whether couples use photography terms precisely.
Carmen asked whether inquiries mentioning that style ever became clients.
Carmen recommended keeping the term under review rather than excluding it immediately.
verify_before_publishing: Confirm permission for an anonymized call example.
Omit the unpublished booking counts from the client's answer.
angles.why_selected: This gives WIA a wedding-specific opinion with a clear expert contribution. It can reach photographers through a familiar language question while showing how Carmen makes Google campaign decisions. It is stronger than a basic negative-keyword lesson because the point is how WIA judges relevance, not which setting to use.

internal_insights.insight: The photographer distinguishes natural wedding coverage from leaving couples without direction. She wants candid moments but knows couples may still want help during portraits. She proposed "authentic, not staged" herself; the excerpt contains no WIA response or confirmed copy revision.
internal_insights.use: Use in the creative review to check that the ad promise matches the service. Confirm any final wording rather than presenting the client's suggestion as a WIA recommendation.

internal_insights.insight: The prospect recognized the setup workload and praised the system, but viewed the recurring commitment differently because she limits her calendar to 20 weddings a year. This is feedback about her buying decision, not evidence that the offer lacks value. No WIA diagnostic question or response appears in the excerpt, and the offer discussed is not identified.
internal_insights.use: Confirm which offer was discussed. Use the exchange internally to understand how limited-calendar owners weigh ongoing support and time savings. Do not turn her budget reaction into public advice, a blanket volume requirement or a claim that the system is only worthwhile for venues and planners.

considered_not_selected.idea: A wedding business can serve two markets while focusing one campaign on one of them
considered_not_selected.reason: Carmen confirmed the intended launch geography, which supports Whitney's belief that "Strategic ads give you control over your points of entry." The possible shift is that advertising can focus on one market without redefining the whole business. However, the photographer supplied the landing-page rationale and chose Orlando; the excerpt does not show WIA weighing the options or recommending the focus. Hold for a fuller strategy exchange.

considered_not_selected.idea: Candid wedding photography can still include gentle direction
considered_not_selected.reason: The client clearly explains the distinction and proposes wording, but no WIA move is recorded. This could shift a couple-facing assumption about candid photography, yet on its own it would market the photographer rather than demonstrate WIA's work. A broader positioning treatment would also overlap the recent UVP content.

considered_not_selected.idea: How we'd use an all-inclusive venue comparison in retargeting
considered_not_selected.reason: Whitney described deeper reasons to choose the venue in retargeting and separately recommended the comparison chart for the landing page. She did not explicitly recommend turning the chart into a retargeting ad. Combining those into a reported campaign decision would go beyond the call. The selected cards preserve the two contributions accurately.

pillar_notes.note: Use the photography-language opinion for reach. Its supporting scene shows Carmen's judgement, so it can introduce WIA without becoming a settings tutorial or an offer pitch.
Use the creative-by-objective explanation as the trust-builder and Tuesday email direction. S1 and S2 offer additional context, but neither warrants another public process card from these excerpts.

Close with the venue comparison recommendation and the week's single Instagram offer CTA, joining the ELEVATE waitlist. Sell the strategic contribution rather than implying the chart was implemented or produced results. S6 remains internal.
